Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> A report published by NielsenIQ on October 19, 2023, identified two major trends in the U.S. tire market based on data from GfK's panel of independent tire retailers. [1] The first trend is the significant impact of increasing Electric Vehicle (EV) adoption, which spurred a 128% growth in EV tire sales during the January to July 2023 period compared to the same timeframe in 2021. [1] Although the EV segment constitutes less than 0.5% of the total tire market, its rapid growth and profitability are notable. [1] The second trend is the emergence of the 'All-Weather' tire category, which has seen its sales grow by 63.4% between the fourth quarter of 2019 and the fourth quarter of 2022, disrupting the traditional winter tire market. [1] This category is particularly gaining traction in U.S. regions with milder winters. [1] <2> Contrary to some reports of a market decline, an analysis published on October 5, 2023, confirmed that US natural rubber (TSR) prices experienced a substantial surge during September 2023. This increase was primarily driven by optimism surrounding the economic outlook in major consumer nations, such as China and India, and favorable trends in crude oil prices. The September price hike followed a positive market turnaround that began in the latter half of August 2023. <3> In June 2023, natural rubber prices in the US and across the globe experienced a significant decline. This depreciation was attributed to several factors, including weak demand from China, the European energy crisis, an import glut, and specific weather conditions. Globally, sluggish demand, fluctuating futures markets, and subdued economic conditions contributed to the plunge. An oversupply from Southeast Asian exporting countries, where monthly output exceeded consumption, also led to a decrease in the price of imported materials to the United States. Some analysts in July 2023 anticipated that prices could decline further in July before potentially trending upward in August. <4> In May 2023, the export dynamics of unvulcanized rubber from the United States showed a notable divergence between price and volume. Following a peak price of $4,531 per ton in April 2023, the export price for unvulcanized rubber decreased by 4.1% to settle at $4,347 per ton in May. [1] In contrast to the price drop, the export volume experienced a significant increase of 14%, reaching 26,000 tons for the month. [1] This surge in volume contributed to a total export value of $113 million for unvulcanized rubber in May 2023. [1] The main destinations for these exports were Mexico, Canada, and India, which collectively accounted for 72% of the total volume. [1] <5> Economic activity in the U.S. manufacturing sector contracted for the sixth consecutive month in April 2023. According to the Institute for Supply Management (ISM), the Manufacturing PMI® registered 47.1 percent in April. This marked the sixth month of contraction following a 28-month period of growth. Among the eleven industries that reported contraction during this period was the Plastics & Rubber Products sector. <6> In February 2023, the price of synthetic rubber in the United States was recorded at $2,802 per ton (FOB, US), which represented a 4.4% decrease from the previous month.

These conditions, linked to the El Niño phenomenon, have included prolonged high temperatures, dry weather, and subsequent excessive monsoon rains and floods, which have disrupted rubber tapping and damaged crops. In Thailand, the world's top producer, output is expected to decline by 10% to 15%. This has led to a significant price surge, with the benchmark Osaka contract hitting a 13-year high. In the Chinese market, prices for RSS1 spot rubber increased from approximately 1800 USD/MT in January to around 1892 USD/MT by March, with further increases to 2060 USD/MT by June 2024. The constrained supply is compounded by strong demand from downstream industries, particularly the tire and automotive sectors. <3> A J.D. Power study released in March 2024 revealed a growing disparity in satisfaction with original equipment tires between electric vehicle (EV) and internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicle owners. [1] The 2024 U.S. Original Equipment Tire Customer Satisfaction Study indicates that EV owners report their tires wear out faster than owners of gasoline-powered vehicles. [1] This accelerated wear is attributed to the greater vehicle weight and higher torque characteristic of EVs. [1] The study suggests a significant opportunity for tire manufacturers and automakers to collaborate on developing tires that meet the specific performance needs of the expanding EV market and to educate consumers about the differences in tire performance. [1, 3] <4> The U.S. Department of Commerce announced the revocation of antidumping (AD) and countervailing duty (CVD) orders on rubber bands from China and the AD order on rubber bands from Thailand. This decision, published in the Federal Register on March 21, 2024, was made because no domestic interested party filed a notice of intent to participate in the five-year sunset reviews of these orders. The revocation for the AD and CVD orders on rubber bands from China is effective as of February 19, 2024, while the revocation of the AD order for rubber bands from Thailand is effective April 26, 2024. Consequently, the U.S. International Trade Commission terminated its reviews. <5> On March 5, 2024, the U.S. Tire Manufacturers Association (USTMA) published its February 2024 forecast, projecting that total U.S. tire shipments would reach 335.7 million units for the year 2024, an increase from the 331.9 million units shipped in 2023. [7] The forecast anticipates a rise in both original equipment (OE) and replacement shipments for passenger and light truck tires. [7] Specifically, OE shipments for passenger and light truck tires are expected to increase by 1.4% and 2.6%, respectively, while replacement shipments for passenger and light truck tires are projected to grow by 0.5% and 2.8%, respectively. [7] <6> A retrospective report on the third quarter of 2023 stated that natural rubber prices saw a steady decline, hitting a low point in September due to weakening global demand and recession concerns. [4] However, this view is not universally supported, as market data from the period indicates a more complex and varied trend. For instance, in the key Chinese domestic market, prices dipped early in the quarter but rebounded sharply in the latter half. [1] Similarly, the United States market experienced a substantial price surge in September following a positive turnaround that began in late August. [2] Price data for the Singapore/Malaysia benchmark also shows the quarter's low point occurring in August, followed by an increase in September. The report anticipated that prices would strengthen in the first quarter of 2024, a forecast driven by expected strong sales from the tire and electronics gadget manufacturing sectors. While the tire industry's demand is a significant factor, the outlook for 2024 was moderated by potential challenges for U.S. consumers, including high-interest rates and stringent credit conditions, which could impact auto and tire sales. The analysis also noted that while supply chain conditions for SBR and tires had improved since 2022, concerns about a structural deficit in semiconductor capacity remained. <8> Goodyear formally announced its 'Goodyear Forward' transformation plan on November 15, 2023, a strategy designed to optimize its portfolio and enhance shareholder value. [9, 13] The plan aims to achieve $1 billion in annualized cost reductions by the end of 2025, with a total of $1.3 billion in benefits when including top-line actions. [9, 15] This is a more ambitious goal than the initially reported $350 million in savings for 2024, which was a projection for that specific year. [10] The total restructuring cost is estimated at approximately $1.1 billion. [9, 15] As part of this global restructuring, Goodyear is closing multiple manufacturing facilities. The company confirmed the closure of its plant in Shah Alam, Malaysia, with manufacturing operations ceasing on June 30, 2024, affecting around 550 employees. [3, 6, 7] Additionally, Goodyear announced the closure of two plants in Germany: the Fulda factory is slated to close by the end of the third quarter of 2025, and tyre manufacturing at the Fürstenwalde facility will be phased out by the end of 2027. [5, 14, 17] These actions in Germany are expected to impact approximately 1,750 jobs. [5] <9> A report published by NielsenIQ on October 19, 2023, identified two major trends in the U.S. tire market based on data from GfK's panel of independent tire retailers. [1] The first trend is the significant impact of increasing Electric Vehicle (EV) adoption, which spurred a 128% growth in EV tire sales during the January to July 2023 period compared to the same timeframe in 2021. [1] Although the EV segment constitutes less than 0.5% of the total tire market, its rapid growth and profitability are notable. [1] The second trend is the emergence of the 'All-Weather' tire category, which has seen its sales grow by 63.4% between the fourth quarter of 2019 and the fourth quarter of 2022, disrupting the traditional winter tire market. [1] This category is particularly gaining traction in U.S. regions with milder winters. [1] <10> Contrary to some reports of a market decline, an analysis published on October 5, 2023, confirmed that US natural rubber (TSR) prices experienced a substantial surge during September 2023. This increase was primarily driven by optimism surrounding the economic outlook in major consumer nations, such as China and India, and favorable trends in crude oil prices. The September price hike followed a positive market turnaround that began in the latter half of August 2023.
